title: Plans and options: direct, regular, growth, IDCW, folio, NFO
objectives: Explain direct vs regular plans and growth vs IDCW options without jargon.
Say why a ₹10 NFO is not cheaper than a ₹200 fund.
body_md:
Every scheme comes in a direct plan (bought straight from the AMC, no distributor commission) and a regular plan (bought through a distributor, commission included in the expense ratio). Separately, the growth option reinvests profits so they show up as a rising NAV, while the IDCW option pays out of the investor's own capital and gains, so the NAV falls by the payout.

| Term | Plain meaning | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Direct plan | Bought straight from the AMC; no distributor commission, so a lower expense ratio | Same portfolio, slightly higher NAV growth over time |
| Regular plan | Bought through a distributor; includes distributor commission in the expense ratio | Client pays for advice and service through the expense ratio |
| Growth option | Profits stay invested and show up as a rising NAV | Best for long-term wealth building |
| IDCW option | Income Distribution cum Capital Withdrawal (old name: dividend). Payouts come out of the investor's own capital and gains; NAV falls by the payout | ₹1 per unit paid → NAV drops by ₹1 |
| Folio number | Your account number with an AMC; all your investments in that AMC can sit under one folio | Quote it for any service request |
| NFO (New Fund Offer) | The launch period of a new scheme, usually at ₹10 per unit | A ₹10 NFO is not "cheaper" than an existing fund at ₹200 |
example: A fund pays IDCW of ₹1 per unit: the NAV drops by ₹1. The payout is not extra income; it came out of the fund.
say: The growth and IDCW options of one scheme hold the same portfolio; only what happens to profits differs.
A regular plan costs more because it includes commission for guidance and service.
never: IDCW is a bonus on top of your returns.
This NFO is cheap because its NAV is only ₹10.

check.q: When an IDCW of ₹1 per unit is paid, the NAV:
check.why: Falls by ₹1. The payout comes out of the fund's assets.

check.q: Direct and regular plans of a scheme differ in:
o: Only the expense ratio, which includes distributor commission in the regular plan
check.why: The difference is the expense ratio, which includes distributor commission in the regular plan.
